topic: Staying active over the Christmas break

slides.headline: Five ways to keep moving this break
slides.sub: Holidays change your routine. Your body still likes regular movement.

slides.title: 1. Keep one anchor habit
slides.body: Pick one thing you'll do most days, like a morning walk or ten minutes of exercises. One small habit is easier to keep than a full routine when every day looks different.

slides.title: 2. Swap, don't stop
slides.body: Gym closed or away from home? Swap in a beach walk, a swim, a bike ride or a bodyweight session. Your tissues care about regular load more than where it comes from.

slides.title: 3. Move between long sits
slides.body: Long drives, flights and marathon lunches add up. Get up every 30 to 60 minutes where you can. A lap of the backyard or a stretch at a rest stop counts.

slides.title: 4. Go easy on the new stuff
slides.body: Holidays bring new activities: cricket on the beach, long hikes, paddleboarding. Start with a shorter version and build up. Sore the next day is common, so plan an easier day after.

slides.title: 5. Beat the heat
slides.body: Move early or late in the day, carry water and wear a hat. In very hot weather, shorter or indoor sessions are a sensible swap.

slides.headline: Want a plan for the new year?
slides.body: Our team can help you keep moving over the break or pick things up again afterwards. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
The Christmas break shakes up every routine. Your body still likes to move. ☀️

You don't need a perfect holiday program. One anchor habit, like a morning walk or ten minutes of exercises, goes a long way when every day looks different.

Swap rather than stop, get up between long drives and lunches, ease into new activities like beach cricket or paddleboarding, and move early or late on hot days with plenty of water.

If a niggle flares over the break, or you want a plan for the new year, our team at Hybrid Physiotherapy can help. Book online via the link in bio.

story.headline: Holiday routine out the window?
story.body: Keep one anchor habit: a morning walk or ten minutes of exercises. Small and daily beats big and rare.
